description: The exact CPV filter syntax and URL parameters of the ÚVO 'Vyhľadávanie zákaziek' interface and the EVO OrderSearch were not established.
No contracting-authority shortlist yet for banking/payments demand (which SK public bodies actually buy acquiring, card issuing, cash logistics, ATM services, core-banking IT).
ÚVO review/appeal decisions (rozhodnutia, námietky, revízne postupy) were not located as a distinct browsable source in this pass.

Cell was scoped to the public/statutory channel; utilities-sector obstarávatelia and state-owned enterprises procuring payment acceptance (transport operators, Slovenská pošta, energy utilities) were not specifically probed.
English coverage of this cell is thin and mostly low-quality commercial tender-lead sites.
The actual number and character of Slovak banking/payment notices on TED is unknown — no counts by CPV, year, buyer type or winner were established.
No agreed CPV code list for 'banking and payments' has been fixed for this run; scouting used ad-hoc codes (66110000, 66172000, 72212442).

Notices published under the utilities/defence directives and under concessions use different eForms notice subtypes; these were not examined and may carry payment/cash-handling contracts of Slovak state entities.
This cell covers Slovak buyers, but Slovak/CEE payment vendors also win contracts published by buyers in other member states; those notices would be missed by a buyer-country=SVK filter.
TED only carries above-threshold contracts; a large share of Slovak banking/payment procurement (especially municipal and small-agency card/POS/cash services) will sit below EU thresholds.
Reuse conditions were not confirmed for ECEPP, the F&T Portal and opentender.eu; only TED/data.europa.eu are clearly open-reuse.

EU-funded Slovak projects (Recovery and Resilience Plan, Partnership Agreement 2021-2027) generate procurement announced through national EU-funds portals rather than TED when below threshold; these were not scouted here.

EU-level oversight actors touching SK procurement — OLAF, EPPO (Slovakia participates), European Court of Auditors, and the CJEU/General Court on SK infringement cases — were not searched in this pass.

Domestic financial-control actors other than NKÚ — Ministerstvo financií SR (Sekcia auditu a kontroly / vládny audit), Úrad vládneho auditu, and managing authorities' irregularity findings on EU-funded contracts — are unmapped.
Criminal-side oversight (Generálna prokuratúra SR, NAKA / Úrad boja proti korupcii, Špecializovaný trestný súd) which prosecutes procurement manipulation was not covered.
No machine-readable API or bulk export was confirmed for ÚVO decisions, PMÚ decisions, or NKÚ reports; NKÚ's list uses Liferay portlet pagination and ÚVO decisions are PDFs on fileadmin paths.
English-language coverage of this cell is thin: ÚVO, NKÚ and PMÚ publish substantive decisions almost exclusively in Slovak; only EU-level pages provide EN framing.
Historical depth of the ÚVO decision registers (how far back the online listings reach, and what moved to /dohlad/archiv) was not established.

No CPV code shortlist for banking and payments has been fixed. uvostat.sk exposes per-CPV pages (e.g. /cpvkod/{id}) and TenderRadar filters by CPV, but the specific CPV branches covering financial services, banking software, payment terminals/POS, ATMs, card issuance and related IT services were not enumerated in this pass.

The e-procurement execution platforms named by aggregators — EKS (Elektronický kontraktačný systém, elektronické trhovisko), JOSEPHINE, ERANET — were identified only indirectly, through third-party aggregators. Their own open-data/API surfaces were not investigated in this cell.

No archival/snapshot strategy was identified for notices that are delisted from the official portal, nor for defunct civil-society mirrors (znasichdani.sk). Web-archive coverage of Slovak procurement sites was not assessed.

Joining suppliers across ÚVO notices, CRZ contracts, OCDS records and company registers relies on IČO and on OCDS ocid, but no mapping between the identifier schemes used by uvostat.sk, Ekosystém.Slovensko.Digital and the OCDS publication was established.

Re-use terms were not read in full for the commercial/semi-commercial analytics layers (uvostat.sk, transparex.sk, transpera.sk, tendermonitor.sk, tenderradar.sk) or for the Slovensko.Digital premium tier.

Municipal and self-government contract registers outside CRZ (the ~130 smaller registers that OtvorenéZmluvy aggregated, plus commercial register services such as eGovZmluvy/zmluvy.egov.sk) were touched only in passing.
Member rosters of SBA, Slovenská FinTech asociácia, FINAS, ITAS and RÚZ were identified by URL but not individually fetched and parsed in this pass.
Payment/e-money providers passported into Slovakia from other Member States will not appear in SK-only registers.

This cell concentrated on supplier/actor registers; the contracting-authority side (ÚVO Register verejných obstarávateľov, state IT bodies, municipalities, Štátna pokladnica) was only touched via one URL.

No searches were run for stavebné sporiteľne, credit unions, crypto/VASP registers, or the Slovak Association of Insurance Companies, each of which may carry its own membership or licence list touching payments.
Regional/secondary outlets and aggregators not yet assessed: SME/Index SME, Pravda ekonomika, Euractiv.sk, TASR/teraz.sk, PC Revue/Nextech, Startitup, Zastavme korupciu.
No systematic mapping yet of the named journalists and procurement lawyers who repeatedly break SK bank/state IT tender stories, nor of their personal blogs/LinkedIn/X accounts.
No decision recorded on subscribing to the paywalled titles that carry the highest-value content.
Commercial-bank procurement (non-public) has no journalistic watchdog equivalent to Red Flags.

Prípravné trhové konzultácie (statutory pre-tender market consultations under the Slovak public procurement act) were not searched; these are published by contracting authorities and are the most explicit legal pre-announcement of a tender.

State-sector payment-heavy institutions were not individually profiled: Štátna pokladnica, Sociálna poisťovňa, Slovenská pošta, VšZP, DataCentrum MF SR, NASES, Úrad vlády, self-governing regions and Bratislava/Košice city IT units.

Government legislative and cabinet pipelines (rokovania.gov.sk cabinet materials, slov-lex legislative process) were not covered; strategy documents and system mandates are approved there before any budget or tender exists.

Bank-side strategy artefacts (annual reports, Pillar 3 disclosures, parent-group technology plans for Erste/Intesa/RBI/KBC) that name planned payment platform investments were not covered by this cell's pass.

English-language coverage in this cell was thin — most productive material is Slovak-only. EU-level sources (EU Recovery and Resilience Scoreboard country page, Digital Europe Programme work programmes) were only touched indirectly.

Regional self-government (VÚC / samosprávne kraje) and the large state-owned enterprises outside those checked (ŽSR, ZSSK, Slovenská elektrizačná prenosová sústava, vodárenské spoločnosti, VšZP) were not individually scouted, yet each is a significant buyer of card acceptance, cash handling and account services.

No supplier-side index was established mapping SK bank / PSP legal entities (IČO) to their public contracts — the analysis-critical join. Slovenská sporiteľňa, VÚB, Tatra banka, ČSOB, Prima banka, Poštová banka, 365.bank, UniCredit, plus acquirers and terminal vendors were not enumerated with IČOs.

Glossary coverage was built for contract/invoice terminology (zmluva, objednávka, faktúra, dodávateľ, akceptácia platobných kariet, platobná brána, bankomat, hotovostné operácie, ceniny) but not validated against actual CRZ contract-title conventions; Hungarian-minority and English-in-Slovak variants were not tested.

CRZ starts 1.1.2011 and the eGovZmluvy-to-CRZ auto-forwarding only began 1.4.2022; pre-2022 municipal contracts may exist only on the originating platform or in municipal archives (e.g. archivzverejnovanie.bratislava.sk).
Reuse licence for the CRZ bulk export and for the third-party aggregators (Slovensko.Digital Datahub, uvostat, eGovZmluvy) was not confirmed, and Datahub is explicitly freemium with a price list.
Private health insurers Dôvera and Union have no confirmed procurement profile pages yet; their buyer status is subject to a contested ÚVO ruling.
EKS (Elektronický kontraktačný systém) — the SK electronic marketplace used by Sociálna poisťovňa and others for below-threshold contracts — was referenced but not yet profiled as a source.

Buyer-to-platform mapping is only partially established: ERANET (Slovenská pošta), JOSEPHINE and eZakazky (ŽSR), IS EVO (Štátna pokladnica, Finančná správa). Platform of record for MF SR, Sociálna poisťovňa, VšZP and ZSSK not confirmed.
ÚVO bulletin open data on data.gov.sk was referenced second-hand but the actual dataset endpoint was not located in this pass.
English-language coverage of these buyers' procurement is thin — only generic market guides and low-quality commercial tender aggregators surfaced.

Only a sample of municipal buyers was reached (Bratislava, Košice, Prešov, Žilina, Nitra, Humenné, Ružomberok). Slovakia has ~140 mestá, 2,700+ obce, 8 VÚC, 17+22 mestské časti and dozens of dopravné podniky / technické služby.

Cash-collection / cash-in-transit and cash-handling services procured by municipalities (prevoz cenín, spracovanie hotovosti, inkaso miestnych daní a poplatkov) were not directly searched; only ticketing and parking were probed in depth.

ERANET and other smaller e-procurement platforms (11+ exist in SK) expose tenders on per-buyer subdomains that were not enumerated; the tail of platforms beyond Josephine/eZakazky/EKS/ERANET is unmapped.
Hungarian-language publication by southern Slovak municipalities (Komárno, Dunajská Streda, Rimavská Sobota) was not searched, although some bilingual noticeboards exist.
Archives of low-value contracts (e.g. the VUCKE §9(9) archive runs to at least page 17) were identified but not traversed, so no historical baseline of municipal payments spend was established.
No confirmed tendering platform for SZRB, Eximbanka SR or SIH.
No API/open-data endpoint validated for ÚVO (ISEPVO/eForms), CRZ or TED in this pass; all findings rest on HTML.

No CPV code list has been fixed for this cell's technology interests (banknote processing and sorting machines, security printing, ATM/cash equipment, core banking software, payment clearing systems).
PTK (preliminary market consultation) coverage is confirmed only for NBS; it is unknown whether SZRB, Eximbanka or SIH publish PTKs at all.

Not covered: ÚVO revision/appeal decisions (rozhodnutia, námietky) and NKÚ SR audit reports on state financial institutions, both of which expose contested and cancelled tenders — often the most informative cases.
NBS as a Eurosystem NCB may participate in ECB/Eurosystem joint procurement (e.g. banknote-related tenders published by the ECB), which would not surface in Slovak registers at all.

Polish-language search for mBank S.A. supplier/procurement channels ('dostawcy', 'zakupy', 'przetarg', 'portal dostawcy') was not performed; Czech-language search for ČSOB group procurement ('dodavatelé', 'nákup', 'výběrové řízení') was also not performed even though ČSOB SK sits under the CZ/KBC structure.

No check was made of whether SK banks run sourcing through group IT/shared-service subsidiaries that DO publish tenders (e.g. Erste's service companies, KBC Global Services CZ, PB Servis / SKPAY in the 365.bank group, VÚB Generali, Tatra-Leasing).

The Slovak commercial e-sourcing platforms (JOSEPHINE/PROEBIZ, ERANET, TENDERnet, evo.gov.sk, EVOSERVIS) were identified but not systematically queried for bank buyers; whether any of the nine target banks has a buyer profile there is untested.

Two high-yield indirect Slovak registries were not queried in this run: CRZ (Centrálny register zmlúv, crz.gov.sk) and RPVS (Register partnerov verejného sektora, rpvs.gov.sk). Banks and their vendors appear in both, and RPVS discloses beneficial owners of any company contracting with the state.

Vendor-side disclosure was not scouted: technology suppliers routinely publish reference/case-study announcements naming the SK bank that awarded them work, which is often the ONLY public trace of a private-bank RFP outcome.
Private commercial banks and payment institutions as buyers are represented almost entirely by inference; only VÚB and NBS were pinned to concrete procurement pages.
Per-client subdomain instances of ERANET and PROEBIZ were sampled, not enumerated.
ToS / robots.txt and paid-tier licensing terms of the monitoring services (Transpera, TenderRadar, Tender Monitor, ADVAL, tender.sk) were not reviewed.
English-language coverage of this cell is thin because the platforms are overwhelmingly Slovak-only; only generic EN queries were productive.
Independent ATM deployers and non-bank cash operators (IAD model) in Slovakia were not mapped: no operator list, no procurement or supplier channel identified.

CPV codes proposed for filtering (30123600 ATMs, 30162000 smart cards, 79710000 security services, 50000000 maintenance) were inferred, not confirmed against actual Slovak notices for ATM/CIT/terminal contracts.
Commercial bank and acquirer procurement (the bulk of POS, card personalisation and ATM-estate spend) has no public tender channel, leaving A2 monitoring blind to the highest-value deals.

Zákazky s nízkou hodnotou (low-value contracts) — where most individual terminal, kiosk and servicing purchases sit — are dispersed across thousands of buyer websites and EKS, and are not comprehensively covered by any free source found.
ERANET is deployed as many per-buyer instances and only the Slovenská pošta instance was identified; the rest of the instance list is unmapped.
The most analysis-ready SK procurement dataset (UVOstat API) is token-gated with only /api/subjekty free; the rest is paid, and tender.sk is subscription-only.
Ness (Ness Slovensko / Ness KDC Košice), Atos/Eviden SK, DXC, IBM SK, Accenture SK and Deutsche Telekom IT Solutions Slovakia were not individually crawled for banking reference pages.
Payments-specific SK vendors beyond the seed list (e.g. card personalisation bureaus, POS distributors, fintech processors serving Slovak banks) were not enumerated.
Vendor LinkedIn pages, conference/sponsorship materials and job ads (which name bank projects) were not explored as disclosure channels.
No historical archive strategy tested for vendor reference pages that get pruned when contracts end.
Vendor claims are promotional and often anonymised; no cross-check pathway to award records was defined within this cell.
